title: A List of Places to Go: Waypoints With Tolerances, Dwell and Timeouts, Skipping or Giving Up, and Resuming After a Reboot Without Starting Over

questions.question: When is a leg of a waypoint mission reached?
options: When the vehicle first comes within the tolerance
When the vehicle has stopped, wherever it is
When the vehicle is within the tolerance and has stood for the dwell time
When the leg's timeout has passed
questions.explanation: Coming within the tolerance starts the dwell, with the speed held at zero. The leg is done when the dwell is over.

questions.question: How long did the vehicle stand at the waypoint that asked for a dwell?
options: 0.0 s: a dwell only slows it
10.0 s, the timeout of the leg
questions.explanation: The waypoint asked for a dwell, and the vehicle stood for 4.1 s with its speed at zero before the next leg began.

questions.question: With the abort policy the mission ended after:
options: 40 s, when the list ran out
0 s: it refused to start
After the skip policy had tried each leg once
10.0 s, the timeout of the leg
questions.explanation: The vehicle could not move, the first leg ran out of time at 10.0 s, and the abort policy ended the mission there. Skip would have gone on to the next leg.

questions.question: After a restart at the third leg of four, the vehicle drove on the rest of the list:
options: 19.4 m, against 38.4 m starting again
38.4 m, the whole list again
0 m: the mission was already done
19.0 m, half of the whole list
questions.explanation: The leg number and the results were read back from the flash, so legs one and two were not driven again.

questions.question: Why did the car circle the waypoint with a tolerance of 0.10 m?
options: The waypoint was outside the map
A car cannot hit a point finer than its turning circle from any heading
The speed set for the leg was too high
The dwell time was too short
questions.explanation: The point was inside the car's smallest circle, which passes no nearer than 0.68 m. With a tolerance of 0.70 m the car was there in 1.8 s.

questions.question: What happens to the timer of a leg on restore?
options: It carries on from where it was
It is set to the timeout, so the leg ends at once
It is saved with the leg number
It starts again: only the leg and the results are saved
questions.explanation: Only the leg number and each leg's result are written down. A restarted leg gets its full time again.
